text: Community equipment lending is a real coordination problem. Requests arrive in messages, availability gets lost, and a wheelchair can be promised twice. Volunteers need to know what is available, who approved a handoff, and whether an item came back safely. Borrowed Steps is built for that gap.

The audience is a neighborhood volunteer or community equipment room, working with borrowers who need a safe, dignified handoff. The fix is a shared, persisted workflow: request, review, reservation, pickup, return, inspection, and a complete audit trail. Every operational decision remains with a person.

The built in assistant uses the real Strands SDK with Groq to turn an ordinary borrower note into a structured draft. It can point out a missing location or due date, but it is advisory and read only. It cannot approve allocation, choose a conflict winner, or change inventory.

This is the public release: a React interface and FastAPI boundary on Vercel Hobby, durable TLS verified rows in Neon Postgres, and Groq Free for bounded inference. The repository includes the architecture diagram, migrations, setup instructions, tests, and an MIT license. The personal spend target is zero.

In the live app, a volunteer starts a synthetic workspace and sees real inventory with versions and condition states. A structured request captures the borrower, equipment kind, pickup location, and timezone aware due date. The request is visible before any item is reserved.

The volunteer opens the allocation review and explicitly confirms the match. Only that human action creates the reservation. Pickup is a second explicit confirmation, so the system never treats a draft or a button preview as consent.

The same workflow records pickup, return, inspection, and audit events with optimistic versions and idempotency keys. A stale or duplicate action returns a stable conflict instead of corrupting the record. If the model is busy, the deterministic workflow stays usable and the UI says so.

Borrowed Steps turns a fragile chat thread into a trustworthy community handoff. Open the live app at borrowed-steps.vercel.app, inspect the code at github.com/AtchayamG/borrowed-steps, and see the full working story in this public demo.
